rule.description: A named struct type is a god class when it declares at least 8 methods whose signatures and bodies directly depend on at least 4 distinct non-universal collaborator families. A method depends on a family through a qualified identifier (websocket.Accept, webrtc.DataChannel) or through a field or method selection whose owning type is declared in that package (l.svcCtx.CallbackService.UserAfterOnline via *svc.ServiceContext). Universal infrastructure (standard library beyond crypto primitives, protobuf wire format, go-zero framework, project common/ library) and the type's own package are excluded so the rule measures genuine domain collaborators. Implemented with golang.org/x/tools go/analysis (singlechecker).

checks.description: Detect a single connection-owner type that combines transport establishment, cryptographic key negotiation, connection verification/authentication, presence bookkeeping, and pool fan-out writes in one method set.
checks.detected_relation: single named connection-owner type -> >=4 unrelated collaborator families across >=8 declared methods
checks.why_this_is_the_smell: The type centralizes responsibilities that belong to separate cohesive owners, so every transport, security, identity, or fan-out change lands on one class and one set of lock-guarded connection pools.
